concise_summary: PKD argues that his 2-3-74 meta-abstraction was primarily a verification of Platonic Form theory—the realization that the past exists latently in the present—and secondarily a confirmation of apostolic Christianity. He synthesizes Heidegger's diagnosis of the metaphysical Fall (being vs. having Logos) with Cartesian epistemology and Buddhist/Brahmanic cosmology to construct a unified system where consciousness both creates and perceives reality through participation in a macromind (VALIS). The entry traces how his ten-volume opus (especially Ubik) articulated this metaphysics before 2-3-74 externally verified it.
key_claims: Plato's Form theory is true: the past is latently present now, accessible through direct cognitive awareness (pistis), not doctrinal assent.
The metaphysical Fall occurred when philosophy shifted from being-Logos (Parmenides) to having-Logos (Aristotle), and this Fall was reversed in PKD's 2-3-74 experience.
Reality is psychomorphic: the macromind adapts itself to individual conceptions of what is real, adapting to preconceptions while remaining absolutely real.
Ubik embodies the true nature of absolute reality (God/Logos) based on John 1 and YHWH's theophany at Sinai, functioning as salvific revelation.
Humans possess innate Platonic knowledge of God (Cartesian innate categories) that remains theoretical until a triggering stimulus makes it veridical.

Time and change are linked: androids and ossified entities lack cumulative/evolutionary change and thus exist in cyclic, non-linear time, while beings in growth (like Beethoven) participate in true, continuous temporal becoming.
